subject: Staggered top-up amendment & legal checklist
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Staggered top-up amendment draft + legal checklist

Karthik / Laura —

Bluewave got back after our call and wants to move forward with a staggered top-up instead of a single capacity add. They want three monthly increments (Nov/Dec/Jan) with a price slab that steps down after the second top-up. Commercial asked us to leave a narrow reopener for rate review tied to utilization > 85% for 30 days.

I attached a first-pass change order (Bluewave_Staggered_Topup_CO_draft.docx) — it pulls the existing Order Form, adds an Exhibit clarifying deliverables and the staggered schedule, and proposes a fee ladder. Can you both review for two things:

- Commercial / billings: Is the fee ladder language sufficient for invoicing and proration? I included an example calc in the notes but would appreciate a clean formula for the exhibit. (See pricing-model.xlsx)
- Legal: Do we need a standalone amendment effective date vs. ‘effective upon fully executed amendment’? Any gating language you want (e.g., required PO, invoices not billable until PO received)? Also flag any compliance addenda — Bluewave asked if this change triggers a need to re-execute the DPA or SOC2 evidence (they’re in healthcare).

Key asks / timeline:
- Quick legal read + bullet redlines by EOD Friday (Nov 13) so we can share with Bluewave during their procurement window.
- If possible, include recommended DocuSign signatory block and a short boilerplate for phased acceptance (we want each top-up to have a functional acceptance trigger so they can start using capacity immediately).

Link to HubSpot deal is below for context. I’ll loop in Evan from Bluewave after we have a consolidated internal list.

Thanks —
Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 09:14 AM Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com> wrote:
> Bluewave got back after our call and wants to move forward with a staggered top-up instead of a single capacity add.
> 
Thanks for the heads-up. Quick commercial notes after a skim:

- Fee ladder: Prefer explicit unit rates per month with a cumulative discount for months 2+ (e.g., Month1 $X/node-hr, Month2 $X-5%, Month3 $X-10%). This makes invoicing and cost-of-goods tracking cleaner.
- Reopener: OK to include utilization-based reopener but limit it to requests for rate renegotiation (not automatic rate changes). Add a notice and 30-day negotiation window + fallback to current rates until agreed.
- Proration: For top-ups that begin mid-billing-cycle, use "pro rata by day" formula. I'll attach a quick pricing model to illustrate.

Commercial asks for legal:
- Add a clause that each top-up becomes "billable upon deployment and acceptance testing completion" (acceptance = auto-pass after 5 business days if no written rejection).
- Capture who signs the PO (procurement contact) and whether we can invoice prior to PO arrival (our preference: invoice upon signup, but we can withhold if no PO).

I attached pricing-model.xlsx with sample calculations. If Laura can draft the short acceptance / invoice gating language, I’ll take care of the fee ladder numbers and update the Exhibit.

Karthik
Head of Sales, EMEA & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-model.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staggered top-up amendment draft + legal checklist

Diego / Karthik —

Thanks for sending. I reviewed the draft and flagged a few items that should be incorporated before sharing with Bluewave procurement:

1) Effective date / execution: Use an "Effective Date" defined as the date the last Party signs the amendment. That avoids ambiguity about when the reopener clock starts.
2) Acceptance triggers: Redline the acceptance to be: (a) "functional acceptance" after deployment and a 5-business-day observation window; (b) if Bluewave provides a written rejection with the reasonable detail, Redwood will remediate within 10 business days. If remediation fails, Parties will follow dispute resolution in base MSA.
3) Fee ladder / invoicing: Include a short formula in Exhibit (example): "Monthly Fee = Unit Rate x Provisioned Units x Days in Month / 30". Keep simple; do not reference internal cost.
4) Reopener: Make sure the reopener is a negotiation trigger only — require 30 days' written notice and at least one meeting between leadership; do not allow unilateral rate changes.
5) Compliance / DPA: Because Bluewave is healthcare, confirm with Security whether the top-up requires any new data flows. If no new data processing aside from existing environment, DPA stands. If they request logs retention beyond our standard, that should go into the DPA addendum.
6) Signatories & DocuSign: Add signatory blocks for both parties and include a clause that the amendment may be executed in counterparts and via electronic signature. I'll attach a short legal checklist and a sample signatory block.

Proposed sample clause to add under "Amendment Execution":
"This Amendment shall become effective as of the date of the last signature ("Effective Date"). Each Top-Up shall be provisioned in accordance with the schedule in Exhibit A and shall be deemed Accepted pursuant to the Acceptance criteria set forth herein. Invoicing for each Top-Up will commence on the provisioned date and will be prorated if provisioned for a partial month."

If that looks fine, I can paste my redlines into the Word draft and then we can produce a clean final for Evan. Also, please ask Security to confirm the DPA question — I don't want to gate the amendment on SOC2 evidence unless Security flags it.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: legal_checklist.pdf (pdf, 42KB)

Thanks for the conversation last week. Attached is the final amendment reflecting the staggered top-up schedule (Exhibit A), the fee ladder Karthik and I discussed, and the acceptance / invoicing language Laura recommended. Key points summarized below:

- Billing: Unit rate by month with proration for partial months; invoicing begins on provisioning/acceptance as described in the amendment
